Leland Orser's Top 10 Movies, Ranked

Discover the top 10 movies featuring Leland Orser, ranked for their impact and his memorable performances. From thrilling crime dramas to intense action films, explore why these movies are must-watch classics.

Originally published 25 February 2025 · RewindZone Archive

Actor & Director ProfilesLists & RecommendationsActionDramaCrime

Leland Orser is a renowned character actor celebrated for his ability to bring depth to a wide range of roles. While he may not always be the main star in his films, his performances always leave a lasting impression on audiences. With a career spanning over three decades, Orser has shown his talent in everything from intense thrillers to thoughtful dramas. In this article, we rank Leland Orser's top 10 movies, highlighting his notable roles and their impact on cinema. Whether you enjoy gripping crime thrillers or moving dramas, this list showcases the best of Leland Orser's impressive career.

10. The Bone Collector (1999)

Director: Phillip NoyceGenre: Crime Thriller

The Bone Collector is a gripping crime thriller based on the novel by Jeffery Deaver. The film stars Denzel Washington and Angelina Jolie as they hunt a serial killer in New York City. I've always admired how Leland Orser brings depth to his roles, and his portrayal of Richard Thompson, a forensic technician, is no exception. Though not the lead, Orser's character is crucial to the story, showing his expertise and dedication to solving the case. His performance shows his ability to play complex characters with skill. The film's intense plot and great cast make it a standout in the crime thriller genre, earning it the #10 spot on our list.

9. Confidence (2003)

Director: James FoleyGenre: Crime, Thriller

Confidence is a clever and engaging con artist film directed by James Foley. The movie features a dynamic cast, including Edward Burns, Rachel Weisz, and Dustin Hoffman, who all deliver compelling performances as they navigate a world of deception and high-stakes cons. Leland Orser plays Lionel Dolby, a character whose actions greatly influence the plot.

I particularly enjoy how Orser brings a sense of unpredictability to his role, making Lionel Dolby a character you can't help but watch closely. His performance adds layers to the film's story, keeping the audience on the edge of their seats. The clever twists and turns, combined with the strong cast, make Confidence a thrilling watch, securing it the #9 spot on our list.

8. Blindspotting (2018)

Director: Carlos López EstradaGenre: Drama, Comedy

Blindspotting is a powerful film that blends social commentary with drama and comedy. Directed by Carlos López Estrada, the movie stars Daveed Diggs and Rafael Casal, who also co-wrote the script. Leland Orser plays Officer Clark, a character whose presence adds tension and complexity to the story.

What stands out to me about Orser's performance is his ability to portray authority figures with depth. His character, Officer Clark, is not just a typical antagonist but a complex individual who challenges the main characters in meaningful ways. The film's exploration of gentrification, race, and identity is both thought-provoking and entertaining, making Blindspotting a deserving entry at #8 on our list.

7. Saving Private Ryan (1998)

Director: Steven SpielbergGenre: War, Drama

Saving Private Ryan is an iconic war film directed by Steven Spielberg, known for its intense and realistic portrayal of World War II. The movie features a stellar cast, including Tom Hanks and Matt Damon, and is renowned for its powerful storytelling and emotional depth. Leland Orser plays Lieutenant DeWindt, a character who contributes to the film's authenticity and emotional impact.

I find Orser's performance particularly compelling because he brings a sense of realism to his role, making the character relatable and grounded. His portrayal adds to the film's overall impact, which is both moving and thought-provoking. The film's gripping narrative and exceptional performances make Saving Private Ryan a timeless classic, earning it the #7 spot on our list.

6. Alien Resurrection (1997)

Director: Jean-Pierre JeunetGenre: Sci-Fi, Horror

Alien Resurrection is a thrilling sci-fi horror film directed by Jean-Pierre Jeunet, set in the iconic Alien universe. The movie stars Sigourney Weaver, Winona Ryder, and features Leland Orser as Purvis, a character who adds to the film's tension and suspense.

I appreciate how Orser's performance brings a sense of urgency and realism to his role, making Purvis a memorable part of the story. His ability to show fear and desperation in dangerous situations is impressive. The film's amazing visual effects and action sequences, combined with the strong performances, make Alien Resurrection a standout in the sci-fi horror genre, securing it the #6 spot on our list.

5. Runaway Jury (2003)

Director: Gary FlederGenre: Thriller, Drama

Runaway Jury is a compelling legal thriller directed by Gary Fleder, based on the novel by John Grisham. The film features an impressive cast, including John Cusack, Gene Hackman, and Dustin Hoffman, who deliver powerful performances in a gripping courtroom drama. Leland Orser plays Lamb, a character whose actions significantly impact the story.

I've always been captivated by legal thrillers, and Orser's performance in Runaway Jury is a standout. He brings a sense of intensity and complexity to his role, making Lamb a character you can't help but watch closely. The film's compelling narrative and strong performances make it a must-watch, earning it the #5 spot on our list.

4. Taken (2008)

Director: Pierre MorelGenre: Action, Thriller

Taken is an action-packed film directed by Pierre Morel, starring Liam Neeson as a former CIA operative on a mission to rescue his daughter from kidnappers. Leland Orser plays Sam Gilroy, a character whose presence adds depth to the narrative.

I've always enjoyed action films that keep you on the edge of your seat, and Taken certainly delivers. Orser's performance as Sam Gilroy is noteworthy for its intensity and authenticity. He brings a sense of urgency and realism to his role, making the character memorable. The film's fast-paced action and compelling storyline make it a thrilling watch, securing it the #4 spot on our list.

3. Se7en (1995)

Director: David FincherGenre: Crime, Thriller

Se7en is a dark and chilling crime thriller directed by David Fincher, known for its gripping narrative and outstanding performances by Brad Pitt and Morgan Freeman. Leland Orser delivers a small but impactful role that significantly contributes to the film's tense atmosphere.

I find Se7en to be one of those films that stays with you long after the credits roll. Orser's performance, though brief, is often cited as one of the best performances by an actor in a single movie scene. He brings an intensity and authenticity to his role that adds depth to the film's chilling narrative. The film's dark themes and powerful storytelling make it a standout in the crime thriller genre, earning it the #3 spot on our list.

2. The Guest (2014)

Director: Adam WingardGenre: Thriller, Action

The Guest is a thrilling film directed by Adam Wingard, known for its unique blend of suspense and dark humour. The movie stars Dan Stevens as a mysterious soldier who visits the family of a fallen comrade. Leland Orser plays Potter, a character whose interactions with the main character add tension and intrigue to the story.

I particularly enjoy how The Guest keeps you guessing until the very end. Orser's performance as Potter is compelling, bringing a sense of authority and suspicion to his role. His ability to convey complex emotions in high-pressure situations is impressive. The film's clever plot twists and strong performances make it a standout in the thriller genre, securing it the #2 spot on our list.

1. Faults (2014)

Director: Riley StearnsGenre: Drama, Thriller

Faults is a captivating psychological drama directed by Riley Stearns, known for its compelling storytelling and excellent character development. Leland Orser takes the lead as Ansel Roth, a man grappling with personal and professional crises, and he absolutely nails the role.

I find Faults to be a deeply engaging film that explores complex themes with skill and depth. Orser's portrayal of Ansel Roth is nothing short of exceptional, showcasing his ability to convey a range of emotions and internal struggles. His performance is a testament to his skill as a character actor, making Faults a must-watch and securing it the #1 spot on our list.
